OpenRLHF is the first easy-to-use, high-performance open-source RLHF framework built on Ray, vLLM, ZeRO-3 and HuggingFace Transformers, designed to make RLHF training simple and accessible:

RLHF training spends 80% of the time on the sample generation stage. Powered by [vLLM](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm) and Auto Tensor Parallelism (AutoTP), OpenRLHF delivers high-throughput, memory-efficient samples generation. Native integration with HuggingFace Transformers ensures seamless and fast generation, making it the fastest RLHF framework available.

Incorporates advanced PPO tricks inspired by practical guides and community best practices, enhancing training stability and reward quality in RLHF workflows. Referencing [Zhihu](https://zhuanlan.zhihu.com/p/622134699) and [Advanced Tricks for Training Large Language Models with Proximal Policy Optimization](https://hijkzzz.notion.site/rlhf-implementation-tricks?v=158d9a33ecc98132bf9e000c39227361).

# durations=0 will display all tests execution time, sorted in ascending order starting from from the slowest one.
1.  **High-Performance Training**: Supports efficient training in various modes by connecting Megatron with SGLang;

slime's design goal is to make these two capabilities reinforce each other without turning the system into a heavy stack of disconnected trainers, rollout services, and agent frameworks. Megatron training, SGLang rollout, custom data generation, reward computation, verifier feedback, and environment interaction all flow through the same training / rollout / Data Buffer path.
- **Direct engine integration**: Megatron arguments are available directly; SGLang arguments use the `--sglang-` prefix.

Use Megatron arguments directly for parallelism, optimizers, checkpoints, and model configuration. Prefix installed SGLang arguments with `--sglang-`; for example, `--mem-fraction-static` becomes `--sglang-mem-fraction-static`.
- [SGLang Config](docs/en/advanced/sglang-config.md): YAML configuration for server groups, multiple models, and per-group overrides.
- [slime: An SGLang-Native Post-Training Framework for RL Scaling](https://lmsys.org/blog/2025-07-09-slime/)
- **training (Megatron)**: Responsible for the main training process, reads data from the Data Buffer, and synchronizes parameters to the rollout module after training.

- **rollout (SGLang + router)**: Generates new data (including rewards/verifier outputs) and stores it in the Data Buffer. Custom generate functions can wrap this with multi-turn loops, tool calls, environment/sandbox interaction, and verifier-based reward.

[Miles](https://github.com/radixark/miles) is an RL post-training framework for large-scale models, built on slime by [RadixArk](https://github.com/radixark). It stays closely aligned with slime's upstream development while extending it with enterprise-oriented features: deeper [SGLang](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang) integration, operational tooling, deployment support, and optimizations for new [models](https://www.radixark.com/miles/docs/models) and [hardware](https://www.radixark.com/miles/docs/platforms). Miles also adds a growing set of production features, including LoRA, TITO, and low-precision training.

[**vime**](https://github.com/vllm-project/vime) is a post-training framework built on slime and maintained by the vLLM project. It keeps slime's Megatron training stack, Data Buffer dataflow, and custom data-generation design, with its main change being a rollout backend swapped to [**vLLM**](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm) with [vllm-router](https://github.com/vllm-project/router). Starting from an existing slime launch script, adjusting only rollout-related parameters is enough to quickly run training with vime.

[**Relax**](https://github.com/redai-infra/Relax) (Reinforcement Engine Leveraging Agentic X-modality) is an omni-modal agentic RL framework open-sourced by the RedAI Infra team, built upon the slime infrastructure stack that combines Ray, Megatron-LM, and SGLang. Relax adopts a service-oriented architecture on Ray Serve with Megatron-LM and SGLang as training/inference backends. It uses [TransferQueue](https://github.com/Ascend/TransferQueue) to fully decouple Actor, Rollout, ActorFwd, Reference, and Advantage computation onto independent GPU clusters, and introduces **DCS (Distributed Checkpoint Service)** — an NCCL-broadcast weight-sync engine that streams updated Actor weights to Rollout
1.  **Megatron arguments**: slime reads Megatron arguments directly. You can configure Megatron by passing arguments like `--tensor-model-parallel-size 2`.

2.  **SGLang arguments**: All arguments for the installed SGLang are supported through pass-through. These arguments must be prefixed with `--sglang-`. For example, `--mem-fraction-static` should be passed as `--sglang-mem-fraction-static`.
│  └─ slime/rollout/sglang_rollout.py  Sample generation and reward computation
└─ slime/backends/megatron_utils/actor.py
├─ model.py                    Megatron model execution

On a first pass, treat `slime/utils/arguments.py` as the configuration entry point. The deployment details in `slime/backends/sglang_utils/` and the weight-sync implementations under `slime/backends/megatron_utils/update_weight/` can also wait until you need to change those areas.
- Special thanks to the following projects & communities: SGLang, Megatron‑LM, mbridge, OpenRLHF, veRL, Pai-Megatron-Patch and others.

🍔 In addition, ms-swift integrates the latest training technologies, including Megatron parallelism techniques such as TP, PP, CP, EP to accelerate training, as well as numerous GRPO algorithm family reinforcement learning algorithms including: GRPO, DAPO, GSPO, SAPO, CISPO, RLOO, Reinforce++, etc. to enhance model intelligence. ms-swift supports a wide range of training tasks, including preference learning algorithms such as DPO, KTO, RM, CPO, SimPO, ORPO, as well as Embedding, Reranker, and sequence classification tasks. ms-swift provides full-pipeline support for large model training, including acceleration for inference, evaluation, and deployment modules using vLLM, SGLang, and LMDeploy

- **Hardware Support**: Supports NVIDIA GPUs (A100/H100/RTX series, etc., via CUDA), AMD GPUs (MI300 series, etc., via ROCm), domestic hardware such as Ascend NPU, MetaX GPU and Moore Threads GPU (via MUSA), as well as Apple MPS and CPU.
- **Distributed Training**: Supports distributed data parallelism (DDP), device_map simple model parallelism, DeepSpeed ZeRO2 ZeRO3, FSDP/FSDP2, and Megatron distributed training technologies.

- 🥥 **Megatron Parallelism**: Provides TP/PP/SP/CP/ETP/EP/VPP parallel strategies to significantly boost **MoE model training speed**. Supports full-parameter and LoRA training methods for 300+ pure text large models and 100+ multimodal large models. Supports CPT/SFT/GRPO/DPO/KTO/RM training tasks.

- **Inference Acceleration**: Supports Transformers, vLLM, SGLang, and LmDeploy inference acceleration engines, providing OpenAI interfaces for accelerating inference, deployment, and evaluation modules.
- **Model Quantization**: Supports quantization export for AWQ, GPTQ, FP8, and BNB. Exported models support inference acceleration using vLLM/SGLang/LmDeploy.

objective_configuration.advantage_normalization: not executed: injected fixed +1/-1 per-sequence advantages expanded to tokens

friction.description: DeepSpeed source build selected CUDA compatibility probes even with DS_BUILD_OPS=0; CUDA_HOME is absent. Supported DS_ACCELERATOR=cpu plus DS_BUILD_OPS=0 built the real package. No fake backend imports were used.
Installed real FlashAttention exposes OpenRLHF Triton cross_entropy; CPU Actor scoring fails with CPU tensor pointer error. Unmodified native scoring/backward succeeded on CUDA under shared flock.

Nested null for known-disabled clipping/optimizer was treated as an unknown state by conditions.known. Original reports/captures were preserved; fresh explicit_disabled_views use disabled/not-executed strings and validate.

Requesting installed distribution metadata for an uninstalled source checkout made the first successful OpenRLHF symbol import report fail at metadata lookup. Editable no-deps installation provided genuine metadata; final ordered probe completed.

ms-swift top-level requirements allowTRL>=0.15,<1 but GRPOConfig requiresTRL>=0.26. Initial actual constructor attempt failed withTRL0.25.1; retry with0.26.2 constructed the real trainer and executed its loss/backward.

First Swift attempt captured a no-grad rescoring call separately from the loss forward. A new exact-capture attempt uses a pass-through native-scorer wrapper during public compute_loss; prior attempts remain preserved.

The final Swift replay gives both trajectories the identical eight-token prompt, making one complete two-completion GRPO group. Earlier fixed-batch attempts with distinct prompts are preserved as component probes and are not the final group comparison.

The official OpenRLHFv0.9.0 Transformers4.57.0 pin is yanked onPyPI for setup issues; its installed wheel executed. Ray2.59 differs from the framework full-trainer pin2.48 and no Ray trainer was run. These are subset native-component checks, not a fully provisioned trainer environment.
friction.evidence: repair_install_cpu_deepspeed.log and final/deeper native entrypoint logs

allowed_implementation_differences: OpenRLHF uses the native Actor score transform/Triton cross_entropy and PolicyLoss; reference uses Transformers logits, torch.log_softmax, and an independent clipped PPO formula.
Swift uses its native model loader, real GRPOTrainer and TRL selective_log_softmax; reference uses direct Transformers loading/log_softmax and independent sequence-mean GRPO reduction.

Native Swift forwards logits_to_keep=5/use_cache=False as supported by the model; full-sequence reference forwards the same input IDs/positions/masks. The separate row-retention probe did not reduce the initial rescoring discrepancy; no cause is asserted.
OpenRLHF cases use token-mean PPO; Swift uses its actual sequence-mean GRPO reduction. These cases are independently matched to their references, not cross-framework loss comparisons.
common_conditions: Identical checkpoint files and exact FP32 initial parameter hash per matched pair.
Fixed2 trajectories,7 active action targets including2EOS targets; native mask retained.
Identical injected detached old scores and advantages per pair; no reward model or rollout recomputation.
Full parameter inventory including tied-weight mappings; no gradient clipping or accumulation beyond one batch.
TinyQwen2 has a stateless matched explicit SGD(lr0.001,momentum0) step with stored before/after tensors.
All comparison contracts thresholds=null; no pass/fail precision threshold is invented.
coverage_limits: No framework train() loop, training_step() or distributed optimizer step.
Injected advantages do not validate reward normalization or native group-statistic construction.
No fused-Liger, ring/sequence/tensor/pipeline parallel, DeepSpeed engine, Ray worker or Megatron training execution.
One pretrained Llama architecture and one explicitly random tinyQwen2 architecture; Swift executed the pretrained architecture only.
reusable_candidates: A prepared-trajectory adapter that maps native action positions/masks/EOS into target-score artifacts.
A generic native-call pass-through capture wrapper for exact objective scores without replacing native operators.
A prerequisite matrix separating source constraints, import probes, CLI initialization, native model/loss execution and full training.
An artifact metadata convention for explicitly disabled optimizer/clipping states rather than unknown null fields.

export.scope: Native measured statistics and coverage retained; omitted NPY/model arrays prevent full numeric replay from this archive alone.
